rationale.conceptual: The model and dynamics are well-documented, but implementing Langevin integration on a lattice with periodic boundary conditions, proper saturation detection, and computation of correlation functions with disorder averaging requires careful attention and understanding of statistical physics methods.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of 3‑4 sequential steps (generate disorder, run dynamics, compute width and correlation) using only standard libraries (numpy). Inputs are generated in-code, and output are simple CSV files. No external tooling or multi‑stage orchestration is needed.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper implements a standard zero-temperature Langevin dynamics for a 2D random sine-Gordon model. The method is established but requires careful implementation of the integration, disorder averaging, and saturation detection. The conceptual difficulty is moderate (non-trivial but not novel). The execution pipeline is straightforward (generate, simulate, post-process) with only a few steps and no complex tooling, so execution is low-to-moderate. Resource needs are modest: CPU-only, small memory, no external data.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Largest lattice is 512×512 with a few hundred time steps; storing a few snapshots and runtime arrays requires <2 GB RAM. No external dataset; disorder is generated on the fly.
